newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Jan U.S. housing starts seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Jan U.S. housing starts seen rebounding.

text.p: U.S. housing starts data should show a rebound in January from December when bad weather, especially in the Pacific Northwest, took a toll, economists said.
On average, economists polled by Reuters expected an annual rate of 1.42 million starts in January, up from 1.329 million in December.
Housing starts will be released by the Department of Commerce at 830 EST/1330 GMT on Thursday.

"We're expecting a rebound in housing due to the weather. California was dry and that's so important for this number," said Charles Lieberman, director of financial markets research at Chase Securities Inc.
Lieberman's forecast was right in line with most economists at 1.42 million on an annualized basis.
Weather was the most unfavorable for the statistic in the Northeast, as it typically is during the winter, he said.
Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc., also called for an annualized start rate of 1.42 million following the weak December figure.
"Underlying conditions are stronger. We have a tight labor market and low interest rates, ideal for housing starts," Moran said.
David Resler, chief economist at Nomura Securities International Inc., saw housing starts improving about 5.5 percent from December, to a level at about 1.40 million annual starts.
"We think housing in general will be weaker this year than last. But on balance it's a tough call to make in the winter, the West saw some of the worst storms it has had in a century," Resler said.
